assessment_summary: The proof attempts to build a subset $S \subseteq W_{m-1}$ of size $n/2$ with no neighbors in $W_m$. It correctly notes that the set $R_{m-1}$ has no neighbors in $W_m$. However, in the case where $|R_{m-1}| < n/2$, it extends $R_{m-1}$ by adding arbitrary vertices from $W_{m-1}$ to form $S$. In lines 0061-0062, the proof fallaciously concludes that this extended set $S$ also has no neighbors in $W_m$ "since $S \supseteq R_{m-1}$, and by construction $R_{m-1}$ has no edges to $W_m$". Adding vertices to a set can only increase its neighborhood, so the new vertices added to $S$ might very well have neighbors in $W_m$. This invalidates the claim that $N(S) \subseteq V \setminus W_m$, breaking the core contradiction of the proof.
